question: What is the main purpose of Community-Based Rehabilitation (CBR) models in regions with limited specialized infrastructure?

options.A: Replacing tertiary hospitals with commercial pharmaceutical outlets
options.B: Decentralizing care by training local health workers and families to provide basic support
options.C: Enforcing strict institutionalization for every child with a disability
options.D: Transferring all special children to international research institutions

explanation: CBR models bring essential therapy and monitoring closer to rural populations by empowering local healthcare workers and family members. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h6)

question: What environmental hazard is created by the open-air burning of medical plastics and PVC packaging?

options.A: Immediate soil alkalization that prevents plant growth
options.B: Depletion of the local groundwater table
options.C: Release of toxic dioxins and furans into the atmosphere
options.D: Generation of radioactive particulate fallout

explanation: Low-temperature or open burning of chlorinated plastics creates dangerous chemical pollutants that persist in the environment and harm human health. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h4)

question: A community health nurse is conducting an outreach in a rural settlement. Which tool is most practical for rapidly screening toddlers for severe acute malnutrition?

options.A: Advanced body composition analyzer
options.B: Endoscopic visual assessment
options.C: Fasting blood glucose meter
options.D: MUAC color-coded tape

explanation: The MUAC tape is portable, inexpensive, and fast, making it ideal for field outreaches where heavy clinical scales are impractical. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h3)

question: A breastfeeding mother at six weeks postpartum visits a community clinic requesting a contraceptive that will not interfere with breastmilk production. Which method is most appropriate to discuss?

options.A: Progestin-only injectable or lactational amenorrhea method
options.B: Combined hormonal skin patches
options.C: Combined estrogen-progestin oral contraceptive pills
options.D: High-dose emergency contraceptive pills taken daily

explanation: Progestin-only methods and LAM do not compromise milk supply or composition, unlike estrogen-containing contraceptives. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h7)

question: What is the primary function of a night hospital service?

options.A: Isolating violent offenders from the general community permanently.
options.B: Offering secure accommodation and supervision during evening and night hours.
options.C: Delivering electroconvulsive therapy exclusively at midnight.
options.D: Providing daytime employment for unemployed psychiatric patients.

explanation: Night hospitals give individuals a safe place to sleep and receive night-time medication while allowing them to live normally during the day. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T5#GNS314_U5_T5_h3)

question: How does the legal framework surrounding the formulary directly protect hospital patients?

options.A: By guaranteeing free lifetime healthcare services in public facilities
options.B: By automatically granting nursing staff prescribing authority
options.C: By eliminating all out-of-pocket expenses for prescription drugs
options.D: By restricting listed medications to those with verified quality and efficacy

explanation: Regulated formularies ensure that only approved, high-standard medications reach clinical settings, safeguarding patients from falsified products. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T5#GNS215_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which characteristic defines innate immunity?

options.A: It develops slowly only after vaccination
options.B: It requires previous exposure to become active
options.C: It creates highly specific antibodies for one antigen
options.D: It acts rapidly and lacks immunological memory

explanation: Innate immunity is non-specific, acts immediately upon pathogen entry, and does not improve with repeated exposures. [learn more](GST114_U4_T6#GST114_U4_T6_h2)
